costs.limits: Process high-water RSS includes unique material retention, post-timing byte accounting and serialization. Version difference is retained as a negative result; these data do not locate selector peak/production heap or attribute the entire increase to caches.

limits: No exact pre-selection task snapshot exists. Final task is never represented as historical pre-state.

Cursor controlled changes only scheduling.cursor using actual sequence4918; fresh-deferrals also empties scheduling.deferred. All routeRetries, final failed route, plan rows, evidence, unknown fields and pause state are retained.

Read-only selector with memory event sink. Complete submitted event payloads are compared in order; the sink adds no wall-clock at or SQLite sequence. No actual SDK recovery, provider/browser, task-event SQLite writes, or total real-run performance claim.

RawReturns retains first complete result per unique read key (128.65 MB material in cursor case). Peak process RSS includes this instrumentation and serialization, not production eight-entry LRU usage. The observed RSS increase remains a negative comparison result and is not attributed entirely to cache changes.
Absolute times may include GC and profile perturbation; only three unprofiled AB pairs form the paired summary.
The actual fixed task has no active unknown attempts. Unknown behavior is established by separate product/protocol tests, not invented here.
